title: Erdős #401: Factorial Divisibility with Prime Products

problemStatement.formal: Does there exist a function $f(r)\to\infty$ such that for infinitely many $n$ there are $a_1,a_2$ with $a_1+a_2>n+f(r)\log n$ and $a_1!a_2! \mid n!\,2^n3^n\cdots p_r^n$?
problemStatement.plain: Does the extra product of prime powers 2^n 3^n ... p_r^n allow two factorial factors to exceed the usual n+O(log n) barrier by an unbounded multiple of log n?

currentState.nextAction: Formalize the Barreto-Leeham construction or keep the solved result explicitly axiom-backed.
